# OnPager Provider

The OnPager provider manages configuration through the Control API. It supports
teams, services, memberships, integrations, routing, escalation, delivery catalog
bindings, schedules, work calendars, identity and access configuration,
notification templates, outgoing webhooks, suppression and enrichment.

Data sources read existing users, teams, services, roles, groups and known delivery
channels. Required permissions are listed on each reference page.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11.0, < 2.0.0"

  required_providers {
    onpager = {
      source = "onpager/onpager"
    }
  }
}

# Supply values through variables or use the ONPAGER_* environment fallback.
provider "onpager" {
  endpoint = var.onpager_endpoint
  token    = var.onpager_token
  timezone = var.onpager_timezone
}

variable "onpager_endpoint" {
  description = "Control base URL. Null uses ONPAGER_ENDPOINT."
  type        = string
  default     = null
}

variable "onpager_token" {
  description = "Control bearer token. Null uses ONPAGER_TOKEN."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  default     = null
}

variable "onpager_timezone" {
  description = "Optional IANA request timezone. Null sends no override."
  type        = string
  default     = null
}
```


`endpoint` is the Control base URL, including an optional reverse-proxy prefix.
Requests append `/v1`. `token` accepts a Control user PAT or service-account bearer
token. Provider arguments take precedence over environment variables; omitted or
`null` arguments use `ONPAGER_ENDPOINT` and `ONPAGER_TOKEN`. HTTPS verifies server
certificates; requests have a 30-second timeout.

Optional `timezone` sends `Onpager-Timezone` for either token type. The API
interprets local datetime input and formats timestamps; explicit offsets retain
absolute instants. An omitted timezone leaves the API actor's default unchanged.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `endpoint` (String) OnPager Control base URL, including an optional reverse-proxy path prefix. Accepts a literal, input variable or data-source expression known during planning. Omission or `null` uses `ONPAGER_ENDPOINT`; an empty string is invalid. Explicit values override the environment. Use an HTTP(S) URL. HTTPS verifies TLS certificates by default.
- `timezone` (String) Optional IANA request timezone, such as `Europe/Moscow` or `UTC`. Sends `Onpager-Timezone` for both user PATs and service accounts, overriding the profile for this request without changing stored preferences. Omission or `null` sends no header: user tokens use their profile/tenant default, service accounts use UTC. Empty, invalid and unknown values are errors. The backend interprets local datetime input and formats responses; the provider does not convert time zones. Explicit timestamp offsets still identify absolute instants. Recurrence, source weekdays and storage retain their UTC semantics.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) OnPager bearer token, preferably for a service account with explicit native role assignments. Accepts a literal, input variable or data-source expression known during planning, including a Vault secret. Omission or `null` uses `ONPAGER_TOKEN`; an empty string is invalid. Explicit values override the environment. Marked sensitive to hide normal display.

## Data Sources

- [User](data-sources/user.md): UUID, local login or exact email.
- [Team](data-sources/team.md): UUID or exact name.
- [Service](data-sources/service.md): UUID or exact name, with optional expected owner.
- [RBAC role](data-sources/rbac_role.md): UUID or stable key.
- [Group](data-sources/group.md): UUID, stable key or unambiguous name.
- [Delivery channel](data-sources/delivery_channel.md): known UUID and metadata.
